An important thing I would add is to have each class be equally viable in an equal number of situations.

For example, utility based characters often get looked over, because either they're reliant on long fights (and nobody wants to spend 10 minutes on a random encounter) or they're resource heavy. Giving them special attacks that deal massive damage to disabled enemies is a good idea to work a class around. Otherwise, they're usually only useful against bosses.

I never liked the idea of an all-weapon specialist. Makes him seem like a multi-purpose filler, and takes away your strategy for team building. Often times you can just have one healer and then fill the rest of your spots with guys like this, and beat the entire game with this lame-ass party.

I like the idea of a risk/reward class like warlocks. Like having all spells cost health while giving him life drain with damage, stuff like that.
Or maybe inflicting debuffs on him causes him to gain power. Sleep causes him to release a nightmare that is the equivalent of Rage. Silence gives him access to an alternate ability list. Blind causes him to counter attack without ever missing. Poison causes him to regenerate energy equal to the damage he takes. And then give him powers that inflict both enemies and himself with these debuffs for an insane character class.

Those are all very good points. We're open to rethinking these classes. These are definitely just initial thoughts, and I would agree that a multipurpose character kind of turns into one that is required to do well.

One issue I see is the blandness of a heavy weapon specialist. What kind of commands could he do to make him feel unique? Burst damage and slow speed is very simple, and consumable dependent playstyles are vilified in games. I'm not entirely sure how I would make heavy weapons seem fun and complicated.
Maybe if the Marauder got increased turn rate when he kills someone, a friend dies, or when he's at low health, and have attacks that consume health for bonus effects? I dunno. I would just suggest that you avoid making any of the classes too simple. People like complicated and they like being rewarded for figuring out how to do cool stuff.

Thinking about it, I'm unsure what the conceptual differences between smuggler and assassin would be. Both would probably be close ranged, debuff specialists with a focus on agility. If either heavily use debuffs, what's separating them from the Tesla or the Harbinger? If they don't, then what makes them different from any other damage class?

All very good points. A lot of the distinguishing factors will be their their stats and scaling of health/energy/etc. And the idea behind the attributes such as Sooth and Tech are that they provide a separate, slow growing resource that is used for abilities beyond a basic attack.

I agree though. That's why we're trying to do this survey, so we can get some ideas of unique abilities, and then kind of refine them down. I was already have a challenging time thinking of unique abilities between classes that differ by more than just name.
